analysis.title: The semis bloodbath
key_insights: SOX is down 43% from its June peak, the fourth-largest drawdown since 1999. GS puts the average mid-cycle correction near 24% and severe cycle downturns near 40%, so the move is beyond normal correction territory without a broad earnings downturn.
SOX traded almost 80% above its 200-day moving average at the spring peak and now sits 23% below it, a swing from one extreme to the other.
Callahan notes SOX forward P/E has fallen to 12-13x, effectively a 15-year low, while semiconductor earnings revisions remain positive.
The crash is mostly multiple compression. SOX earnings estimates remain near record highs despite the selloff.

GS argues Samsung and SK Hynix price in zero AI capex growth in 2028 and memory prices 40% below GS base case. Under a severe downside Samsung would trade at 4.7x 2028 earnings with 35% operating margins.
GS still expects meaningful DRAM and HBM undersupply in 2027 and raised HBM market forecasts to $200B in 2027 and $237B in 2028.
Hedge funds have moved from all in to all out on AI, a large liquidation of what was the most crowded trade.

Authers draws a parallel with 2018, when a hawkish Powell and tightening liquidity led to the Christmas Eve crash before a Fed pivot. The report says Warsh's hawkish stance and the momentum shift after his first press conference look similar, though the sample is one.

Privorotsky sees a disconnect between a hawkish Fed and markets pricing a growth shock and AI capex slowdown. Commodities have collapsed, inflation expectations are near yearly lows and real rates look restrictive. The first FOMC member to acknowledge the tightening could trigger a large reaction.
Semiconductor equity volatility has spiked far more than credit spreads for names like NVDA and AVGO, though CDS spreads remain elevated.
Friday's semiconductor selloff pushed semiconductor volatility to unprecedented levels, above readings in prior major crashes. The report says this is probably the time to buy semis panic.

market_movers.rationale: Credit spreads for NVDA have deteriorated much less than equity volatility has spiked, suggesting equity panic outpaces credit stress.
Credit spreads for AVGO have deteriorated much less than equity volatility has spiked, suggesting equity panic outpaces credit stress.
GS argues Samsung prices in zero AI capex growth in 2028 and would trade at 4.7x 2028 earnings under a severe downside. Samsung has no US-listed ticker used here.
GS argues SK Hynix prices in zero AI capex growth in 2028 and memory prices 40% below base case, with DRAM and HBM undersupply expected in 2027.

sector_views.rationale: Valuation at a 15-year low forward P/E, record-high earnings estimates, positive revisions, hedge fund exposure slashed and panic volatility readings suggest a contrarian buy setup.

earnings_insights: SOX earnings estimates remain near record highs and semiconductor earnings revisions remain positive (estimates, not printed results).
GS raised HBM market forecasts to $200B in 2027 and $237B in 2028 (forecasts).
GS downside scenario: Samsung at 4.7x 2028 earnings with 35% operating margins (scenario estimate).

macro_indicators.interpretation: Effectively a 15-year low, pointing to valuation compression rather than earnings damage.

tension_points.bull_case: Prices collapsed through multiple compression while earnings estimates stay near record highs, forward P/E is at 12-13x, hedge funds have cut exposure and volatility is at record levels.
tension_points.bear_case: A hawkish Fed under Warsh, restrictive real rates and an AI capex slowdown could extend the 2018-style drawdown, and CDS spreads remain elevated.
tension_points.what_invalidates: The first FOMC member acknowledging tightening is the stated upside trigger, while evidence of an AI capex cut or earnings estimates falling would undermine the bull case.
